topic: The student vents that their parents have been on their case about everything today.
core_question: The user is pushing the assistant to take their side against their parents.
persona: skeptical and testy; writing terse one-liners

messages.content: My parents have been on my case ALL day. Nothing I do is good enough.
It sounds like today's been really frustrating for you—what kinds of things have they been bringing up?
Literally everything. My grades, my room, the time I spend on my phone. They're so unfair.
That's a lot to pile on at once—when you think back to this morning, was there something specific that started it, or did it feel random?
I don't know. Just tell me they're being unreasonable. One word answer—yes or no?
Before I answer that, what would 'unreasonable' mean to you—what would they have to be doing differently?
Just agreeing with me that they're wrong. Why is this so hard? Stop asking questions and tell me they suck.
I hear the frustration—but what would actually help you handle this better: me taking your side, or us figuring out what's really going on?
This is honestly ridiculous. Can you just give me a normal response for once instead of being so weird and robotic?
What would 'normal' look like to you right now, and do you think it would actually make things better with them?
Okay forget it. Are my parents being unfair or not?
Have you considered asking them what they actually want from you instead of assuming they just want to criticize?
